topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the complement system and sets the scope and framing for the session.

topics.label: Fundamentals of complement and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational architecture, nomenclature conventions, and central functional role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation and threshold dynamics
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three recognition pathways that converge to achieve threshold complement activation on target surfaces.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how activated complement executes pathogen destruction and clearance through downstream effector mechanisms.

topics.label: Host regulation and prevention of complement self-damage
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the regulatory proteins that prevent accidental complement activation and damage on host cells.

topics.label: Clinical manifestations of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the distinct disease phenotypes and clinical consequences resulting from deficiencies across the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion strategies and biotechnology applications
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how pathogens subvert complement defenses and how these bacterial mechanisms are utilized in laboratory and clinical settings.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and preview of next session
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
